rule: Source code formatting uses 4-column tab stops with tabs preserved (not expanded to spaces)
notes: Each logical indentation level is one additional tab stop; applies to all core C code

rule: Curly braces for controlled blocks (if, while, switch) go on their own lines following BSD layout conventions
notes: Enforced across all backend C source files before release

rule: Line length limited so code is readable in an 80-column window, except where breaking long string literals impairs readability
notes: Soft limit; long error message strings should not be broken arbitrarily

rule: C++ style // comments are prohibited in C code; use /* ... */ comment blocks
notes: pgindent automatically converts // comments to /* ... */

rule: Indented multi-line comment blocks preserved from reflow by adding dashes: /*---------- ... ----------*/
notes: Column 1 comment blocks preserved as-is; indented blocks reflowed without dashed box

rule: Code must only rely on C11 standard features; variable length arrays (VLAs), intermingled declarations, and universal character names prohibited
notes: Portable C11 baseline ensures cross-compiler compatibility

rule: Static inline functions referencing backend-only symbols like CurrentMemoryContext must be wrapped in #ifndef FRONTEND
notes: Prevents unresolved symbol link errors when header is included from frontend utilities

rule: Signal handlers must only call async-signal safe functions, access volatile sig_atomic_t variables, or invoke SetLatch()
notes: Prevents deadlocks and memory corruption on interrupt; wake main loop via latch

rule: Simple function pointer variables must be called with explicit dereference (*func_ptr)(args)
notes: Ensures visual distinction between static function call and indirect pointer invocation

rule: Automated code formatting enforced with pgindent using pg_bsd_indent and pinned perltidy 20230309
notes: Pinned perltidy version required because different versions make different formatting decisions

rule: Perl scripts and modules validated for syntax and style with src/tools/perlcheck
notes: Validates all Perl build scripts and regression test suites

rule: All changes must pass regression tests via pg_regress / meson test
notes: Automated regression tests run on Linux, macOS, FreeBSD, and Windows in CI

rule: Patches submitted as git format-patch to pgsql-hackers mailing list and registered in CommitFest
notes: CommitFest tracks reviewer assignments and committer sponsorship

rule: Contributions must be licensed under the PostgreSQL License (BSD-style permissive license) without conflicting restrictions
notes: Core code must remain under PostgreSQL license without copyleft contamination

rule: Source code is dedicated to the public domain; no copyright or license header may ever be added to any file
notes: Author blessing comment at the top of each file must be preserved unchanged

rule: Open source, not open contribution: pull requests reviewed only as proof-of-concept prior to core developer reimplementation

rule: Canonical version control uses Fossil (https://sqlite.org/src), not Git; git mirrors must use check-in UUIDs from manifest.uuid

rule: Build system configure script uses autosetup, not GNU Autoconf

rule: Generated files must never be edited by hand (sqlite3.h, parse.c/h, pragma.h, opcodes.h/c, sqlite3.c amalgamation)

rule: C89 and C99 compatible C only; no C++, no STL, no exceptions, no variable-length arrays (VLAs)

rule: Dynamic memory allocation must strictly use sqlite3Malloc, sqlite3_malloc64, or sqlite3MallocZero, never raw malloc/calloc

rule: Integer widths must use i64 (sqlite3_int64) for 64-bit values, u32/u64 for unsigned; avoid bare long or int for values exceeding 2GB
notes: Prevents 32-bit signed integer overflow and platform-specific long width bugs

rule: Functions return SQLITE_OK (0) on success and SQLITE_* error code on failure; deferred OOM checking uses db->mallocFailed

rule: Liberal use of assert() for invariants; condition macros ALWAYS(x) and NEVER(x) used for unprovable invariants

rule: 100% branch test coverage (TH3 / MCDC test harness) verified before any official release

rule: Unit and short tests must pass via `make test` and `make test-short`
notes: Tests executed in GitHub Actions across multiple Go versions

rule: Contributors must claim issues before working by commenting on GitHub issue to prevent duplicate effort
notes: Community workflow coordination

rule: Substantial changes must be discussed on prometheus-developers mailing list first; check non-goals list
notes: Avoids implementing rejected features or non-goals

rule: PR descriptions should address a suitable maintainer using `@maintainer` from MAINTAINERS.md
notes: Facilitates reviewer routing across subsystems

rule: Source code licensed under Apache 2.0; file headers must retain standard Apache copyright notice
notes: Validates license headers on all Go files

rule: Metric naming and PromQL syntax changes subject to strict stability guarantees
notes: Prevents breaking existing monitoring dashboards and alert rules

rule: Every commit must have DCO 1.1 sign-off ('Signed-off-by: Real Name <email>') via git commit -s; no pseudonyms or anonymous
notes: Validates DCO compliance

rule: Group logical changes into individual commits; do not mix bug fixes, refactoring, and new features in one commit
notes: Keeps commits bisectable and backportable

rule: Commit title limited to 72 characters, imperative mood, prefixed with subsystem/module (e.g. `mds: ...`, `osd: ...`, `doc/mgr: ...`)
notes: Subsystem prefix mandatory for all commits

rule: Commit message body must explain both 'what' changed and 'why' it was necessary
notes: Mere statements of the obvious rejected during review

rule: Commits addressing tracker issues must include `Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/XXXXX` line
notes: Automatically updates Ceph Redmine tracker status

rule: C++ code formatting enforced via .clang-format
notes: CI checks format of modified C++ files

rule: Changes must pass unit tests via `make check` / `ninja check`
notes: Local unit tests executed before opening PR

rule: Distributed integration testing performed via Teuthology test clusters
notes: Multi-node cluster tests run before changes merged into main

rule: Kernel client patches (RBD, CephFS) maintained upstream in Linux Kernel and must follow SubmittingPatches-kernel.rst
notes: Kernel patches sent to linux-kernel mailing lists

rule: Backports to stable branches (e.g. nautilus, reef) must follow SubmittingPatches-backports.rst with cherry-pick references
notes: Cherry-pick must reference original commit SHA on main

rule: Every PR must correspond to an ASF Jira ticket at issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK
notes: Must search for existing JIRAs before opening a new one

rule: PR title must strictly follow format `[SPARK-XXXXX][SUB-MODULE] Description` (e.g. `[SPARK-12345][SQL] Fix outer join pushdown`)
notes: Matches Jira issue and sub-module tag

rule: Scala code linted with scalastyle and scalafmt via `dev/lint-scala`
notes: Verifies code formatting and Scala idioms

rule: Python code linted with Ruff (>=0.14.0) and Mypy (>=1.19.1) via `dev/lint-python`
notes: Type checking and PEP 8 formatting enforced on PySpark

rule: Local pre-commit hook runs `./dev/reformat-python` via .pre-commit-config.yaml
notes: Formats Python code before git commit

rule: Contributions licensed under Apache 2.0; author affirms legal authority and license terms
notes: Verified by committers before merge

rule: Unit tests must pass for affected modules via `./build/mvn test` or `./build/sbt test`
notes: GitHub Actions runs comprehensive test matrix

rule: Standalone features that can exist as third-party packages must be developed outside Spark core
notes: Spark core maintains strict scope boundaries

rule: PRs require approval from an Apache Spark committer; committers merge with git merge/squash script
notes: Committer merges with attribution lines

rule: Public API changes in org.apache.spark must maintain binary compatibility rules (Mima plugin check)
notes: Flags accidental binary incompatible bytecode changes

rule: Must sign Linux Foundation EasyCLA at easycla.lfx.linuxfoundation.org before contributing
notes: Pull requests blocked until CLA signature is verified

rule: Smaller spec changes require an approved GitHub issue before opening a PR; unaccepted issues result in PR rejection
notes: Ensures alignment with specification scope

rule: Significant changes (new metric types, new signals, cross-cutting architectures) require an OpenTelemetry Enhancement Proposal (OTEP)
notes: OTEP must reach consensus before specification PR

rule: Prototype requirement: new features require working prototype in a spec-bound SDK; feature stabilization requires prototypes in multiple languages (typically 3)
notes: Prevents abstract specifications without working implementations

rule: Specification written in Markdown with lines wrapped at 80 characters wide
notes: Formatted for readability on GitHub and in terminal browsers

rule: Markdown style validated using .markdownlint.yaml via `make markdownlint`
notes: Enforces headers, list styles, and formatting rules

rule: Prose quality and spelling verified via `make language-analysis` (cspell and textlint)
notes: Autofix prose issues with `make fix`

rule: Hyperlinks validated using markdown-link-check via `make markdown-link-check`
notes: Docker-based link checker flags dead URLs

rule: Requirements must use RFC 2119 keywords (MUST, SHOULD, MAY) carefully and sparingly
notes: Imperatives restricted to true interoperability requirements

rule: PR ready to merge only when approved by 2+ code owners representing at least two distinct companies
notes: Multi-vendor consensus prevents single-vendor dominance

rule: Declarative configuration changes must link to corresponding change in opentelemetry-configuration repository
notes: Config schema and spec must merge simultaneously

rule: All commits must include DCO sign-off ('Signed-off-by: Real Name <email>') via git commit -s
notes: Validates Developer Certificate of Origin on all PR commits

rule: PRs must be opened by a human; automated PR creation requires prior maintainer approval
notes: Unauthorized bot/automation accounts restricted from organization

rule: AI-assisted submissions must be thoroughly reviewed by human author who takes full responsibility for correctness
notes: Prohibits unverified AI output

rule: Dev tools installed via `script/setup/install-dev-tools` and dependencies via `make install-deps`
notes: Pinned tooling matching CI runner images

rule: Local check suite `make check` must pass cleanly before opening or updating a PR
notes: Runs validation scripts, linters, and static checks

rule: Go linting strictly enforced with .golangci.yml (copyloopvar, depguard, dupword, gosec, misspell, modernize, perfsprint, revive)
notes: Verified across all packages

rule: Package dependency boundaries enforced via depguard (denies github.com/opencontainers/runc direct dependency)
notes: Isolates containerd core from libcontainer internals

rule: Direct import of standard ^regexp$ package forbidden in favor of internal/lazyregexp.New via forbidigo
notes: Prevents startup latency overhead from eager regex compilation

rule: Failure injection in integration tests must use the failpoint pattern (internal/failpoint, integration/failpoint)
notes: Enables deterministic simulation of crash and error states

rule: Tests must pass at appropriate level (unit, integration, or e2e)
notes: Verified in GitHub Actions matrix

rule: Review and approvals governed by containerd MAINTAINERS file
notes: Requires approval from maintainers with domain expertise

rule: Pre-proposal requirement: discuss proposed change on a GitHub issue and get maintainer go-ahead before implementing
notes: Unsolicited PRs modifying workflow or language will not be accepted

rule: Moratorium on state storage backends: no new state storage backends accepted in Terraform core repository
notes: Core focuses on maintaining or deprecating existing backends

rule: Moratorium on tool-specific provisioners: vendor provisioners (chef, puppet, salt) are deprecated; PRs for them rejected
notes: Provisioners are tools of last resort

rule: Changelog entries required for user-facing changes created using changie tool (`changie new`)
notes: Validates changelog YAML files in .changes/unreleased/

rule: Changes must include unit tests and, where applicable, acceptance tests against external services (`TF_ACC=1 go test ...`)
notes: Acceptance tests verify real cloud API interactions

rule: Generated code must never be edited by hand; regenerate using `go generate ./...`
notes: CI checks verify generated files match source schemas

rule: Go code must be formatted using standard gofmt and linted with golangci-lint
notes: Checked in GitHub Actions CI workflows

rule: Code review routed according to CODEOWNERS; external maintainers review subsystem changes
notes: Maintainers for specific backends/subsystems must approve

rule: Source code licensed under Business Source License (BSL 1.1); contributions governed by HashiCorp CLA
notes: BSL 1.1 header and HashiCorp contributor agreement

rule: AI usage policy: human author must understand, verify, and take responsibility for all submitted code and tests
notes: Unverified AI submissions rejected

rule: Minor changes to comments or CLI help text not accepted to prevent merge conflicts
notes: Low-value text changes rejected
